# M0-d-05a: closing check of consolidation round C1 (R4) (lane `check/M0-d-05a-consolidate-close-1`, flow flow-7, stage group S, 2026-10-11)

The seat ran in a Claude Code cloud container on 2026-10-11 from 21:01 to about 23:40 UTC: Opus 5.5, Linux x64, Node
v24.12.0. The machine check printed `linux:Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz:4cpu:16gib`, which matches the brief.
`tools/test_budget.py` printed 1 before each run (and `--mutants` 1), so every vitest run used `--maxWorkers=1` and the
mutants ran one at a time. The seat is an implementer-side closing checker. It wrote no part of the item: it is not the
author (L-0122), a fixer (L-0126; L-0440 for this round's `build/M0-d-05a-consolidate-1`) or an earlier checker (L-0124,
L-0131). Its ledger row is L-0446 in `CLEAN-ROOM.md` §2.

How the seat worked:

* It changed no file of the item. It wrote this file, rows N-c2-1 and N-c2-2 of `checks/M0-d-05a-notes.md`, its
  CLEAN-ROOM row, its two landed records and its lane-log lines. It ran no git command. The verdict file is
  `checks/M0-d-05a-c1.md` (J269); `checks/M0-d-05a.md` stays as committed.
* **The before tree, without git.** The builder's before-mirror was deleted; a copy of the eight item files as they
  stood before the round is in the scratchpad (`d05a-before/`). The seat did not take it on trust: it hashed each file
  as a git blob (`sha1("blob <n>\0" + bytes)`, Python) and compared it with the blob id that `.git/index` records for
  the committed file, read by a Python parser (no git command). **8 / 8 equal**: six files changed by the round
  (`lineage.ts`, `address.ts`, `mint.ts`, `lineage.test.ts`, `address.test.ts`, `mint.test.ts`), and `index.ts` and
  `city.test.ts` are unchanged (the tree's blob equals the index's). The rest of `packages/model` and `packages/tables`
  equals the index except `packages/tables/src/index.ts` (lines 1–2, landed by `build/M0-s-01-fix-s3`, not this item).
* **Its own mirror** (`scratchpad/waves/check-M0-d-05a/mirror`): a tar copy of `plat/` without `node_modules` or
  `dist`, installed `--frozen-lockfile --offline` (`Done in 1.5s`). Its eight item files hashed equal to the landed
  record before the runs, and `diff -r` showed its `src/identity` and `test/identity` identical to the tree after the
  mutant sweep. The before sources were placed beside the consolidated ones as `src/identity-before/` for the
  differential probe. The mirror was deleted at the end, `node_modules` first.
* **Disclosure.** The resume grep of the lane log printed the builder's CHECKPOINT and LANDED lines. The seat planned
  its probe and its mutants from the plan's §1.4 ORACLE lists, the first check's mutant tables and the code. It read
  C-0322, L-0440 and the builder's old → new map in `checks/M0-d-05a-notes.md` only after its probe and mutant sweep
  had run. It did not open the builder's self-check folders.

### (3) New findings — none is a blocker

No gate exits non-zero for this item; every listed interface (`LineageKey`, `lineageHash`, `addressOf`, `mint`,
`TOWN_ROOT`, `parseAddress`) is present with its signature (index and barrel name lists identical, `tsc -b` green); no
stub or shortcut; no wrong result on an honest input (0 of 163 000 differ); no clean-room breach; nothing outside
`plat/`. Two tightenings go to `checks/M0-d-05a-notes.md`: **N-c2-1** (the header line says the identity and matching
modules share the helpers; until R5 lands, only the identity module imports them) and **N-c2-2** (`compareLanes`'s new
doc comment names its tie-break role but not its second use, the duplicate-key test at `mint.ts:212`). The builder's
N-c1-1 (bigint, symbol and throwing-`valueOf` inputs now get the field's RangeError instead of the operator's
exception) is confirmed by the seat's corpus (42 / 817, the same three kinds of value, no number among them). That is
not a shift on any input the types admit, so it is no blocker.
